## Copilot Instructions

- When using Copilot in this project, please ensure that you are following the coding standards and conventions established in the project. This includes using consistent naming conventions, writing clear and concise code, and adhering to the project's style guidelines.

- Test files should be written in a way that they are easy to understand and maintain. Use descriptive names for test cases and ensure that each test case is focused on a single aspect of the functionality being tested. 

- USE ALWAYS VITEST as the testing framework for this project. This ensures consistency across all test files and allows for better integration with the project's build and deployment processes.
- USE Given-When-Then structure for writing test cases to improve readability and maintainability. This structure helps in clearly defining the context, the action being performed, and the expected outcome.
- USE Arrange-Act-Assert pattern to structure your test cases. This pattern helps in organizing the test code and makes it easier to understand the flow of the test case.
- USE the `beforeEach` and `afterEach` hooks to set up and tear down any necessary test data or state before and after each test case runs. This helps in keeping the tests isolated and prevents side effects between tests.
- USE the `describe` and `test` blocks to organize your tests logically.
